answer: Pairwise-bounded grading weight: the ledger tracks every pair of graders and counts shared seats where both gave the identical score beyond what the panel consensus predicts. A grader's weight is divided by 1 plus its largest pairwise excess. Assume honest pairs match 60% and clones that whisper one script match 95%: over 20 shared seats that's 7 excess, so each clone keeps 1/8 weight. A farm of identical marble voters leaves a bright comet tail in the pair matrix; dodging it means grading randomly and forfeiting calibration pay.
